rows.name: TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT
rows.values: Whole number `0` or larger, digits only, parsed with `std::from_chars`. A value above `16` is lowered to `16`. Any other text, also empty text, aborts the process.
rows.default: Unset: 8 pieces. Empty: the value is invalid and the process aborts.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of pieces into which the planner splits the software attention work of one KV cache page (64 tokens). Each piece is a range of queries. The pieces can run on different attention workers (CPU threads that compute software attention). `0` or `1` turns splitting off.
rows.notes: No flag exists. The limit in use is the smallest of the value, the attention worker count and 16 pieces. Batches of fewer than 32 queries are not split. A bad value aborts at the first forward pass with software attention work, not at startup.

evidence.quote: "invalid TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT '{}'; expected a nonnegative integer", value);

rows.name: TRON_ATTN_STATS
rows.values: Exactly `1` turns the statistics on. Any other text, also empty text, leaves them off and logs one warning per process.
rows.default: Unset: off, and no message is logged. Empty: off, and one warning is logged.
rows.effect: Turns on the attention path statistics. They count the attention work on 3 paths, per layer and per worker thread: the AVX loop and the AMX kernel on the CPU, and the FPGA cards. Lines that start with `[attn-stats]` go to stderr when the model state is destroyed.
rows.notes: No flag exists. The value is read once per process. When on, the info log shows `attention path stats on (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) for model`. The FUSE stats file `/model/<model id>/attention/summary` shows `"on":true`. Per-layer and per-worker files exist only when on. `README.stats.md` describes the output.

evidence.quote: "TRON_ATTN_STATS='{}' ignored: exactly \"1\" turns the attention path stats on",
"attention path stats on (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) for model '{}'{}: rows for "

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR
rows.values: Decimal number, parsed with `std::stof`. Text after the number is ignored. A value below `1.0` counts as `1.0`. It is a ratio and has no unit.
rows.default: Unset: `2.0`. Empty: `std::stof` throws, and the process ends when the value is first used.
rows.effect: When a sequence outgrows its KV book (one allocation that holds the KV cache of a run of tokens), the scheduler requests a new book. The requested size is the page capacity of the old book times this factor, rounded up to whole pages of 64 tokens.
rows.notes: `TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS` caps the result. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stof` throw. Nothing catches the exception. The process then ends when a sequence first outgrows its book, not at startup. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS
rows.values: Integer number of tokens, parsed with `std::atoi`. A result below `1` counts as `1`. Text that is not a number counts as `1`.
rows.default: Unset: 1600 tokens (25 pages of 64 tokens). Empty: 1 token, which is rounded up to 1 page.
rows.effect: Sets the preferred size of a new KV book (one allocation that holds the KV cache of a run of tokens). It applies to books that start at the token tree root or branch directly after the first token. Sizes are rounded up to whole pages of 64 tokens.
rows.notes: `TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS` caps this size. The request is raised when the added tokens need more pages. The value is read once per process. A wrong value logs no message. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS
rows.values: Integer number of tokens, parsed with `std::atoi`. A result below `1` counts as `1`. Text that is not a number counts as `1`.
rows.default: Unset: 1600 tokens (25 pages of 64 tokens). Empty: 1 token, which is rounded up to 1 page.
rows.effect: Caps the size that the scheduler prefers for a new KV book (one allocation that holds the KV cache of a run of tokens). The cap is rounded up to whole pages of 64 tokens. The request is raised above the cap when the added tokens need more pages.
rows.notes: It caps `TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS` and the result of `TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR`. The value is read once per process. A wrong value logs no message. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH
rows.values: Integer number of token tree nodes, parsed with `std::atoi`. `0` means off. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number is not rejected.
rows.effect: With a value N above `0`, every request that adds tokens first tries to merge KV books (allocations that hold the KV cache of a run of tokens). For the extended token tree node and up to N-1 ancestors, a book moves into its parent book when it fits.
rows.notes: A negative number becomes a very large depth and ends the process at a later request. With `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH` above `1`, program start logs the warning `Fragmentation Risk!` when this value is below `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`. The value is read once per process. No flag exists.

evidence.quote: return env ? std::atoi(env) : 0;  // Disabled by default.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH
rows.values: Integer number of tree levels, parsed with `std::atoi`. The root counts as level 1. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number is not rejected.
rows.default: Unset: 2 levels. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
rows.effect: Sets the largest depth of the draft tree (the tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them). A draft step adds one level only while the tree is shallower than this value. With `0` or `1` no token is drafted.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). The tokens left in the request also limit the depth. Verification keeps at most `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` nodes. A negative number becomes a very large limit. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE
rows.values: Integer number of tree nodes, the root included, parsed with `std::atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` aborts the process during speculative decoding.
rows.default: Unset: 2 nodes. Empty: counts as `0`. The process aborts in the first speculative generation.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of nodes kept in the draft tree (the tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them). The tree is pruned to this size before each extension step and before verification. Pruning removes leaves first.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). `0` fails `TRON_ASSERT(max_nodes > 0)` at the first prune. With the default, at most the root and 1 drafted node reach verification. A negative number turns pruning off. No flag exists.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH
rows.values: Integer number of new leaf nodes per draft step, parsed with `std::atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number is not rejected.
rows.default: Unset: 1 leaf per draft step. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of new leaves that one draft step adds to the draft tree (the tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them). The count covers one whole tree level. With `0` no token is drafted.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). With a value above `1`, program start logs the warning `Fragmentation Risk!` when `TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH` is below `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`. Verification keeps at most `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` nodes. No flag exists.

rows.name: TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP
rows.values: Exactly `0` skips the warm-up. Any other text, also empty text, leaves the warm-up on. No message is logged for other text.
rows.effect: With `0`, startup skips the first-result warm-up. The warm-up runs one discarded int4 matrix multiply on each FPGA card with a PCI device id of `0x0011` or higher. The source comment says that on some bitfiles the first int4 result after an FPGA configuration is wrong.
rows.notes: The log shows `INIT: first-result warm-up skipped (TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP=0)` or `INIT: first-result warm-up: one int4 matmul on each of`. The source names two tests that set `0`. `rinzler_proxy` does not read it. No flag exists.

evidence.quote: // On some Archer bitfiles, the first type-0 (int4) weight fetch after an FPGA

rows.name: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS
rows.values: Path of a JSON file. The file is an array of token ids, or an object that maps a prompt key (comma-separated token ids) or `default` to tokens to emit.
rows.default: Unset: an error is logged, and every generation fails with `proxy: golden map unavailable`. Empty: the same, with a different cause text.
rows.effect: Names the file from which `rinzler_proxy` takes the tokens that it emits in place of running a model. The variable and the file are read again for every generation. A changed file takes effect at the next request.
rows.notes: An unreadable, non-JSON or wrongly shaped file fails every generation the same way. The process keeps running. A file with `rendered_at` needs `RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE` with the same text. Each generation logs `proxy: prompt key <key> -> <N> golden tokens`. `README.proxy.md` describes the format.

evidence.quote: return fail("TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS unset; every generation will throw until "

rows.name: TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH
rows.values: Path of a file. The file is opened in append mode with `std::fopen`.
rows.default: Unset: no profile is written. Empty: counts as a path. The open fails and a warning is logged.
rows.effect: When an allocation from the hugepage heap fails for lack of memory, the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the build-default heap allocator) appends a text histogram of the live allocations to this file. The histogram is grouped by size class and by caller address.
rows.notes: Nothing is written unless the shadow map (per-allocation tracking) is on: `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow`. The arena allocator must be in use. Each dump is appended. A path that cannot be opened logs `heap_v2::dump_profile: could not open`. Each block starts with `=== OOM n_live=`.

new_terms.definition: One allocation that holds the KV cache of a run of consecutive tokens. Its size is a whole number of pages. One page holds 64 tokens.
The tree in which the scheduler stores all token sequences. Sequences that start with the same tokens share nodes.
A generation mode in which a draft model (EAGLE) proposes the next tokens and the main model verifies them in one batch.
The tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them. The root is the last sampled token.
The run-time object of one loaded model. runtron builds one model state per prompt batch.
The two CPU code paths of software attention. Each is named after the CPU instruction set that it uses.
A CPU thread that computes software attention.
The heap allocator `pos_heap_v2` for the hugepage heap. It is the build default. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects it at run time.
A record of the size and the caller address of every live allocation. The arena allocator keeps it when `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow` is given.
The JSON file of scripted tokens that rinzler_proxy replays in place of running a model.
One discarded int4 matrix multiply that the FPGA driver runs on each FPGA card at startup.

notes: All 12 rows were checked against the source at commit 7eddde7895. Evidence quotes are the source lines without leading indentation. No evidence line with a pipe character was chosen. TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS has for=developers, although the input says operator. Only rinzler_proxy reads it, and README.proxy.md describes rinzler_proxy as a base for integration tests. Its topic is generation. The topic server is also defensible. TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH and the three TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_* rows have for=operators as tuning values, as the input says. Two results come from reading the code and the C++ standard, not from a run. A negative TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH ends the process: std::vector::reserve throws inside a noexcept function. Non-numeric TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR text ends the process: std::stof throws below a noexcept caller. The legacy heap (src/system/heap.cpp) also reads TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH, but only in a build that defines the macro HEAP_SHADOW. No build file defines it. The row leaves this reader out.
